    def _resolved_api_call_timeout(self) -> float:
        """Resolve the effective per-call request timeout in seconds.

        Priority:
          1. ``providers.<id>.models.<model>.timeout_seconds`` (per-model override)
          2. ``providers.<id>.request_timeout_seconds`` (provider-wide)
          3. ``HERMES_API_TIMEOUT`` env var (legacy escape hatch)
          4. 1800.0s default

        Used by OpenAI-wire chat completions (streaming and non-streaming) so
        the per-provider config knob wins over the 1800s default.  Without this
        helper, the hardcoded ``HERMES_API_TIMEOUT`` fallback would always be
        passed as a per-call ``timeout=`` kwarg, overriding the client-level
        timeout the AIAgent.__init__ path configured.
        """
        cfg = get_provider_request_timeout(self.provider, self.model)
        if cfg is not None:
            return cfg
        return float(os.getenv("HERMES_API_TIMEOUT", 1800.0))

    def _resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base(self) -> tuple[float, bool]:
        """Resolve the base non-stream stale timeout and whether it is implicit.

        Priority:
          1. ``providers.<id>.models.<model>.stale_timeout_seconds``
          2. ``providers.<id>.stale_timeout_seconds``
          3. ``HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT`` env var
          4. 90.0s default (time-to-first-byte for non-streaming / Codex
             internal-streaming requests; lowered from 300s in May 2026 so
             fallback providers kick in faster when upstream providers
             stall).  The detector still scales up for large contexts in
             ``_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout``.

        Returns ``(timeout_seconds, uses_implicit_default)`` so the caller can
        preserve legacy behaviors that only apply when the user has *not*
        explicitly configured a stale timeout, such as auto-disabling the
        detector for local endpoints.
        """
        cfg = get_provider_stale_timeout(self.provider, self.model)
        if cfg is not None:
            return cfg, False

        env_timeout = os.getenv("HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT")
        if env_timeout is not None:
            return float(env_timeout), False

        return 90.0, True

    def _compute_non_stream_stale_timeout(self, api_payload: Any) -> float:
        """Compute the effective non-stream stale timeout for this request.

        Accepts either the full ``api_kwargs`` dict (Chat Completions or
        Responses API) or a legacy ``messages`` list.  Context-size scaling
        applies the same way to both shapes via
        :func:`agent.chat_completion_helpers.estimate_request_context_tokens`.
        """
        stale_base, uses_implicit_default = self._resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base()
        base_url = getattr(self, "_base_url", None) or self.base_url or ""
        if uses_implicit_default and base_url and is_local_endpoint(base_url):
            return float("inf")

        from agent.chat_completion_helpers import estimate_request_context_tokens
        est_tokens = estimate_request_context_tokens(api_payload)
        if est_tokens > 100_000:
            return max(stale_base, 240.0)
        if est_tokens > 50_000:
            return max(stale_base, 150.0)
        return stale_base

    def _codex_silent_hang_hint(self, model: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
        """Return an actionable hint when this request matches a known
        Codex silent-reject configuration, else ``None``.

        The ChatGPT Codex backend (``chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex``) has
        historically silently dropped certain model requests: the connection
        is accepted but no stream events are emitted and no error is raised.
        The stale-call detector ends the hang, but a generic "timed out"
        message gives the user no path forward.

        This helper substitutes an actionable hint into the stale-timeout
        warning when the request matches a known silent-reject pattern.
        Currently flagged: ``gpt-5.5`` family on the Codex backend.  See
        hermes-agent #21444 for the symptom history.  The upstream backend
        behavior has historically come and gone with ChatGPT entitlement
        changes — the heuristic stays in place as future-proofing even when
        the symptom is dormant.

        Does NOT fix the backend issue.  Only converts an opaque stale-timeout
        into actionable text so users learn the workaround in seconds rather
        than digging through logs.
        """
        if self.api_mode != "codex_responses":
            return None
        is_codex_backend = (
            self.provider == "openai-codex"
            or (
                getattr(self, "_base_url_hostname", "") == "chatgpt.com"
                and "/backend-api/codex" in (getattr(self, "_base_url_lower", "") or "")
            )
        )
        if not is_codex_backend:
            return None
        eff_model = (model if model is not None else self.model) or ""
        model_lower = eff_model.lower()
        # Match the gpt-5.5 family — bare ``gpt-5.5``, ``gpt-5.5-codex``,
        # vendor-prefixed variants like ``openai/gpt-5.5``, and any future
        # ``gpt-5.5-*`` SKU.  Anchor at a word boundary on either side so
        # unrelated tokens like ``gpt-5.50`` do not match.
        if not re.search(r"(?:^|[/\-_])gpt-5\.5(?:$|[\-_])", model_lower):
            return None
        return (
            f"Codex backend appears to be silently rejecting {eff_model!r} "
            "on chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (no stream events, no error). "
            "This is a known backend-side pattern that has affected ChatGPT "
            "Plus accounts intermittently. "
            "Workaround: try `gpt-5.4` on the same OAuth profile, or `gpt-5.3-codex`, "
            "or switch to a different model/provider in your fallback chain. "
            "Some ChatGPT Codex accounts do not support `gpt-5.4-codex`. "
            "See hermes-agent#21444 for symptom history."
        )

    def _anthropic_prompt_cache_policy(
        self,
        *,

        api_mode: Optional[str] = None,
        model: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> tuple[bool, bool]:

        return anthropic_prompt_cache_policy(self, provider=provider, base_url=base_url, api_mode=api_mode, model=model)

    @staticmethod
    def _model_requires_responses_api(model: str) -> bool:
        """Return True for models that require the Responses API path.

        GPT-5.x models are rejected on /v1/chat/completions by both
        OpenAI and OpenRouter (error: ``unsupported_api_for_model``).
        Detect these so the correct api_mode is set regardless of
        which provider is serving the model.
        """
        m = model.lower()
        # Strip vendor prefix (e.g. "openai/gpt-5.4" → "gpt-5.4")
        if "/" in m:
            m = m.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
        return m.startswith("gpt-5")

    @staticmethod
    def _provider_model_requires_responses_api(
        model: str,
        *,
        provider: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return True when this provider/model pair should use Responses API."""
        normalized_provider = (provider or "").strip().lower()
        # Nous serves GPT-5.x models via its OpenAI-compatible chat
        # completions endpoint; its /v1/responses endpoint returns 404.
        if normalized_provider == "nous":
            return False
        if normalized_provider == "copilot":
            try:
                from hermes_cli.models import _should_use_copilot_responses_api
                return _should_use_copilot_responses_api(model)
            except Exception:
                # Fall back to the generic GPT-5 rule if Copilot-specific
                # logic is unavailable for any reason.
                pass
        return AIAgent._model_requires_responses_api(model)

    def _max_tokens_param(self, value: int) -> dict:
        """Return the correct max tokens kwarg for the current provider.

        OpenAI's newer models (gpt-4o, o-series, gpt-5+) require
        'max_completion_tokens'. Azure OpenAI also requires
        'max_completion_tokens' for gpt-5.x models served via the
        OpenAI-compatible endpoint. OpenRouter, local models, and older
        OpenAI models use 'max_tokens'.
        """
        if self._is_direct_openai_url() or self._is_azure_openai_url() or self._is_github_copilot_url():
            return {"max_completion_tokens": value}
        return {"max_tokens": value}

    @staticmethod
    def _requested_output_cap_from_api_kwargs(api_kwargs: Any) -> Optional[int]:
        """Extract the outgoing response token cap from a prepared request."""
        if not isinstance(api_kwargs, dict):
            return None
        for key in ("max_output_tokens", "max_completion_tokens", "max_tokens"):
            raw = api_kwargs.get(key)
            try:
                value = int(raw)
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                continue
            if value > 0:
                return value
        return None

    def _has_content_after_think_block(self, content: str) -> bool:
        """
        Check if content has actual text after any reasoning/thinking blocks.

        This detects cases where the model only outputs reasoning but no actual
        response, which indicates an incomplete generation that should be retried.
        Must stay in sync with _strip_think_blocks() tag variants.

        Args:
            content: The assistant message content to check

        Returns:
            True if there's meaningful content after think blocks, False otherwise
        """
        if not content:
            return False

        # Remove all reasoning tag variants (must match _strip_think_blocks)
        cleaned = self._strip_think_blocks(content)

        # Check if there's any non-whitespace content remaining
        return bool(cleaned.strip())

    def _strip_think_blocks(self, content: str) -> str:
        """Forwarder — see ``agent.agent_runtime_helpers.strip_think_blocks``."""
        from agent.agent_runtime_helpers import strip_think_blocks
        return strip_think_blocks(self, content)

    @staticmethod
    def _has_natural_response_ending(content: str) -> bool:
        """Heuristic: does visible assistant text look intentionally finished?"""
        if not content:
            return False
        stripped = content.rstrip()
        if not stripped:
            return False
        if stripped.endswith("```"):
            return True
        if stripped.endswith('^'):
            return True
        last = stripped[-1]
        if last in '.!?:)"\']}。！？：）】」』》^':
            return True
        # Emoji ranges (Misc Symbols, Dingbats, Emoticons, Supplemental, etc.)
        if ord(last) >= 0x1F300:
            return True
        return False

    def _is_ollama_glm_backend(self) -> bool:
        """Detect the narrow backend family affected by Ollama/GLM stop misreports."""
        model_lower = (self.model or "").lower()
        provider_lower = (self.provider or "").lower()
        if "glm" not in model_lower and provider_lower != "zai":
            return False
        if "ollama" in self._base_url_lower or ":11434" in self._base_url_lower:
            return True
        return bool(self.base_url and is_local_endpoint(self.base_url))

    def _should_treat_stop_as_truncated(
        self,
        finish_reason: str,
        assistant_message,
        messages: Optional[list] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Detect conservative stop->length misreports for Ollama-hosted GLM models."""
        if finish_reason != "stop" or self.api_mode != "chat_completions":
            return False
        if not self._is_ollama_glm_backend():
            return False
        if not any(
            isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("role") == "tool"
            for msg in (messages or [])
        ):
            return False
        if assistant_message is None or getattr(assistant_message, "tool_calls", None):
            return False

        content = getattr(assistant_message, "content", None)
        if not isinstance(content, str):
            return False

        visible_text = self._strip_think_blocks(content).strip()
        if not visible_text:
            return False
        if len(visible_text) < 20 or not re.search(r"\s", visible_text):
            return False

        return not self._has_natural_response_ending(visible_text)

    def _apply_persist_user_message_override(self, messages: List[Dict]) -> None:
        """Rewrite the current-turn user message before persistence/return.

        Some call paths need an API-only user-message variant without letting
        that synthetic text leak into persisted transcripts or resumed session
        history. When an override is configured for the active turn, mutate the
        in-memory messages list in place so both persistence and returned
        history stay clean.
        """
        idx = getattr(self, "_persist_user_message_idx", None)
        override = getattr(self, "_persist_user_message_override", None)
        if override is None or idx is None:
            return
        if 0 <= idx < len(messages):
            msg = messages[idx]
            if isinstance(msg, dict) and msg.get("role") == "user":
                msg["content"] = override

    def _persist_session(self, messages: List[Dict], conversation_history: List[Dict] = None):
        """Save session state to both JSON log and SQLite on any exit path.

        Ensures conversations are never lost, even on errors or early returns.
        """
        self._drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding(messages)
        self._apply_persist_user_message_override(messages)
        self._session_messages = messages
        self._save_session_log(messages)
        self._flush_messages_to_session_db(messages, conversation_history)

    def _drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding(self, messages: List[Dict]) -> None:
        """Remove private empty-response retry/failure scaffolding from transcript tails.

        Also rewinds past any trailing tool-result / assistant(tool_calls) pair
        that the failed iteration left hanging. Without this, the tail ends at
        a raw ``tool`` message and the next user turn lands as
        ``...tool, user, user`` — a protocol-invalid sequence that most
        providers silently reject (returns empty content), causing the
        empty-retry loop to fire forever. See #<TBD>.
        """
        # Pass 1: strip the flagged scaffolding messages themselves.
        dropped_scaffolding = False
        while (
            messages
            and isinstance(messages[-1], dict)
            and (
                messages[-1].get("_empty_recovery_synthetic")
                or messages[-1].get("_empty_terminal_sentinel")
            )
        ):
            messages.pop()
            dropped_scaffolding = True

        # Pass 2: if we stripped scaffolding, rewind through any trailing
        # tool-result messages plus the assistant(tool_calls) message that
        # produced them. This preserves role alternation so the next user
        # message follows a user or assistant message, not an orphan tool
        # result. Only runs when scaffolding was actually present — normal
        # conversation tails (real tool loops mid-progress) are untouched.
        if not dropped_scaffolding:
            return

        # Drop any trailing tool-result messages
        while (
            messages
            and isinstance(messages[-1], dict)
            and messages[-1].get("role") == "tool"
        ):
            messages.pop()

        # Drop the assistant message that issued the tool calls, if the tail
        # now ends in an assistant-with-tool_calls (the pair that owned the
        # just-popped tool results). Without this, the tail is
        # ``assistant(tool_calls=...)`` with no tool answers, which some
        # providers also reject.
        if (
            messages
            and isinstance(messages[-1], dict)
            and messages[-1].get("role") == "assistant"
            and messages[-1].get("tool_calls")
        ):
            messages.pop()

        """Forwarder — see ``agent.agent_runtime_helpers.repair_message_sequence``."""
        from agent.agent_runtime_helpers import repair_message_sequence
        return repair_message_sequence(self, messages)

    def _flush_messages_to_session_db(self, messages: List[Dict], conversation_history: List[Dict] = None):
        """Persist any un-flushed messages to the SQLite session store.

        Uses _last_flushed_db_idx to track which messages have already been
        written, so repeated calls (from multiple exit paths) only write
        truly new messages — preventing the duplicate-write bug (#860).
        """
        if not self._session_db:
            return
        self._apply_persist_user_message_override(messages)
        try:
            # Retry row creation if the earlier attempt failed transiently.
            if not self._session_db_created:
                self._ensure_db_session()
            start_idx = len(conversation_history) if conversation_history else 0
            flush_from = max(start_idx, self._last_flushed_db_idx)
            for msg in messages[flush_from:]:
                role = msg.get("role", "unknown")
                content = msg.get("content")
                # Persist multimodal tool results as their text summary only —
                # base64 images would bloat the session DB and aren't useful
                # for cross-session replay.
                if _is_multimodal_tool_result(content):
                    content = _multimodal_text_summary(content)
                elif isinstance(content, list):
                    # List of OpenAI-style content parts: strip images, keep text.
                    _txt = []
                    for p in content:
                        if isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("type") == "text":
                            _txt.append(str(p.get("text", "")))
                        elif isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("type") in {"image", "image_url", "input_image"}:
                            _txt.append("[screenshot]")
                    content = "\n".join(_txt) if _txt else None
                tool_calls_data = None
                if hasattr(msg, "tool_calls") and isinstance(msg.tool_calls, list) and msg.tool_calls:
                    tool_calls_data = [
                        {"name": tc.function.name, "arguments": tc.function.arguments}
                        for tc in msg.tool_calls
                    ]
                elif isinstance(msg.get("tool_calls"), list):
                    tool_calls_data = msg["tool_calls"]
                self._session_db.append_message(
                    session_id=self.session_id,
                    role=role,
                    content=content,
                    tool_name=msg.get("tool_name"),
                    tool_calls=tool_calls_data,
                    tool_call_id=msg.get("tool_call_id"),
                    finish_reason=msg.get("finish_reason"),
                    reasoning=msg.get("reasoning") if role == "assistant" else None,
                    reasoning_content=msg.get("reasoning_content") if role == "assistant" else None,
                    reasoning_details=msg.get("reasoning_details") if role == "assistant" else None,
                    codex_reasoning_items=msg.get("codex_reasoning_items") if role == "assistant" else None,
                    codex_message_items=msg.get("codex_message_items") if role == "assistant" else None,
                )
            self._last_flushed_db_idx = len(messages)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Session DB append_message failed: %s", e)

    def _get_messages_up_to_last_assistant(self, messages: List[Dict]) -> List[Dict]:
        """
        Get messages up to (but not including) the last assistant turn.
        
        This is used when we need to "roll back" to the last successful point
        in the conversation, typically when the final assistant message is
        incomplete or malformed.
        
        Args:
            messages: Full message list
            
        Returns:
            Messages up to the last complete assistant turn (ending with user/tool message)
        """
        if not messages:
            return []
        
        # Find the index of the last assistant message
        last_assistant_idx = None
        for i in range(len(messages) - 1, -1, -1):
            if messages[i].get("role") == "assistant":
                last_assistant_idx = i
                break
        
        if last_assistant_idx is None:
            # No assistant message found, return all messages
            return messages.copy()
        
        # Return everything up to (not including) the last assistant message
        return messages[:last_assistant_idx]

    @staticmethod
    def _is_entitlement_failure(
        error_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
        status_code: Optional[int],
    ) -> bool:
        """Detect subscription/entitlement 403s that masquerade as auth failures.

        Returned True only when the body text matches a known entitlement
        shape AND the status is 401/403.  Refreshing an OAuth token cannot
        fix an unsubscribed account, so callers should surface the error
        instead of looping the credential pool.

        Current matches:
          * xAI OAuth: "do not have an active Grok subscription" /
            "out of available resources" / "does not have permission" + "grok"

        Disambiguator for xAI (#29344): the same ``code`` text ("The caller
        does not have permission to execute the specified operation") is
        returned for BOTH an unsubscribed account AND a stale OAuth access
        token.  xAI ships an explicit signal in the ``error`` field that
        tells the two apart: a ``[WKE=unauthenticated:...]`` suffix (and/or
        the ``OAuth2 access token could not be validated`` phrasing) means
        the credentials failed validation — that's recoverable by refreshing
        the token, NOT by surfacing an entitlement message.  When either
        signal is present we return False eagerly so the credential-pool
        refresh path runs, letting long-running TUI sessions recover from
        stale tokens without an exit/reopen cycle.

        Extend here for new providers as we discover them (Anthropic's
        Claude Max OAuth entitlement errors look distinct enough today that
        the existing 1M-context-beta branch handles them; revisit if other
        subscription tiers start producing the same loop signature).
        """
        if status_code not in {401, 403, None}:
            return False
        if not isinstance(error_context, dict):
            return False
        # Build a single lowercase haystack covering every field shape the
        # body might land in.  ``_extract_api_error_context`` normalises to
        # ``message``/``reason``, but callers (and the test suite) may also
        # hand us the raw body with ``code``/``error`` keys; cover both so
        # the WKE disambiguator below fires regardless of entry point.
        message = str(error_context.get("message") or "").lower()
        reason = str(error_context.get("reason") or "").lower()
        code = str(error_context.get("code") or "").lower()
        err = str(error_context.get("error") or "").lower()
        haystack = f"{message} {reason} {code} {err}"
        if not haystack.strip():
            return False
        # xAI's authoritative disambiguator for "stale token" vs
        # "unsubscribed account".  Both conditions share the same
        # permission-denied ``code`` text; only one carries this suffix.
        # Bail out before the entitlement keyword checks so a stale OAuth
        # token routes through the credential-refresh path instead of the
        # surface-error-as-entitlement path.  See #29344 for the long-
        # running TUI failure mode this closes.
        if "[wke=unauthenticated:" in haystack:
            return False
        if "oauth2 access token could not be validated" in haystack:
            return False
        if "do not have an active grok subscription" in haystack:
            return True
        if "out of available resources" in haystack and "grok" in haystack:
            return True
        if "does not have permission" in haystack and "grok" in haystack:
            return True
        return False

    @staticmethod
    def _decorate_xai_entitlement_error(detail: str) -> str:
        """Append a neutral hint when xAI's OAuth surface returns the
        permission-denied 403.

        xAI's ``/v1/responses`` endpoint replies to several distinct failure
        modes with the SAME body::

            {"code": "The caller does not have permission to execute the
             specified operation", "error": "You have either run out of
             available resources or do not have an active Grok subscription.
             Manage subscriptions at https://grok.com/?_s=usage or subscribe
             at https://grok.com/supergrok"}

        That body covers several real causes we cannot distinguish without
        more info from xAI.  The most common (and least obvious) one is
        that **X Premium+ does NOT include API access** — only standalone
        SuperGrok subscribers can use Hermes against xai-oauth.  Lots of
        users see Grok in their X app, assume it works here too, and hit
        this 403 with no idea why.  Lead the hint with that.

        Other possible causes:
          * No Grok subscription at all
          * SuperGrok tier doesn't include the requested model (e.g.
            grok-4.3 may need a higher tier)
          * Monthly quota exhausted (the ``?_s=usage`` URL hints at this)

        Surface the raw xAI text verbatim and point at
        https://grok.com/?_s=usage where the user can see WHICH applies.

        Matched once per detail string — won't double-decorate if the
        upstream already concatenated the same text.
        """
        if not detail:
            return detail
        lower = detail.lower()
        is_entitlement = (
            "do not have an active grok subscription" in lower
            or ("out of available resources" in lower and "grok" in lower)
            or ("does not have permission" in lower and "grok" in lower)
        )
        if not is_entitlement:
            return detail
        hint = (
            " — xAI rejected this OAuth account. NOTE: X Premium+ does NOT "
            "include xAI API access — only standalone SuperGrok subscribers "
            "can use this provider. Other possible causes: no Grok "
            "subscription, your tier doesn't include this model, or your "
            "quota is exhausted. Check https://grok.com/?_s=usage to see "
            "which, or run `/model` to switch providers."
        )
        # Idempotency: detect prior decoration by a substring unique to the
        # hint (not present in xAI's own body text).
        if "X Premium+ does NOT include" in detail:
            return detail
        return f"{detail}{hint}"

    @staticmethod
    def _summarize_api_error(error: Exception) -> str:
        """Extract a human-readable one-liner from an API error.

        Handles Cloudflare HTML error pages (502, 503, etc.) by pulling the
        <title> tag instead of dumping raw HTML.  Falls back to a truncated
        str(error) for everything else.
        """
        raw = str(error)

        if (
            isinstance(error, ValueError)
            and "expected ident at line" in raw.lower()
        ):
            return f"Malformed provider streaming response: {raw[:300]}"

        # Cloudflare / proxy HTML pages: grab the <title> for a clean summary
        if "<!DOCTYPE" in raw or "<html" in raw:
            m = re.search(r"<title[^>]*>([^<]+)</title>", raw, re.IGNORECASE)
            title = m.group(1).strip() if m else "HTML error page (title not found)"
            # Also grab Cloudflare Ray ID if present
            ray = re.search(r"Cloudflare Ray ID:\s*<strong[^>]*>([^<]+)</strong>", raw)
            ray_id = ray.group(1).strip() if ray else None
            status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
            parts = []
            if status_code:
                parts.append(f"HTTP {status_code}")
            parts.append(title)
            if ray_id:
                parts.append(f"Ray {ray_id}")
            return " — ".join(parts)

        # JSON body errors from OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs
        body = getattr(error, "body", None)
        if isinstance(body, dict):
            msg = body.get("error", {}).get("message") if isinstance(body.get("error"), dict) else body.get("message")
            if msg:
                status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
                prefix = f"HTTP {status_code}: " if status_code else ""
                return AIAgent._decorate_xai_entitlement_error(f"{prefix}{msg[:300]}")

        # Fallback: truncate the raw string but give more room than 200 chars
        status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
        prefix = f"HTTP {status_code}: " if status_code else ""
        return AIAgent._decorate_xai_entitlement_error(f"{prefix}{raw[:500]}")

    def _mask_api_key_for_logs(self, key: Any) -> Optional[str]:
        # Azure Foundry Entra ID bearer providers are callables — never
        # invoke them in log paths; identify the auth surface instead.
        if callable(key) and not isinstance(key, str):
            return "<entra-id-bearer>"
        if not key:
            return None
        if len(key) <= 12:
            return "***"
        return f"{key[:8]}...{key[-4:]}"

    def _clean_error_message(self, error_msg: str) -> str:
        """
        Clean up error messages for user display, removing HTML content and truncating.
        
        Args:
            error_msg: Raw error message from API or exception
            
        Returns:
            Clean, user-friendly error message
        """
        if not error_msg:
            return "Unknown error"
            
        # Remove HTML content (common with CloudFlare and gateway error pages)
        if error_msg.strip().startswith('<!DOCTYPE html') or '<html' in error_msg:
            return "Service temporarily unavailable (HTML error page returned)"
            
        # Remove newlines and excessive whitespace

        content = convert_scratchpad_to_think(content)
        content = re.sub(r'\n+(<think>)', r'\n\1', content)
        content = re.sub(r'(</think>)\n+', r'\1\n', content)

    def _redact_message_content(content):
        """Apply secret redaction to message content (str or list-of-parts).

        shape where ``content`` is a list of ``{"type": "text", "text": ...}``
        / ``{"type": "image_url", ...}`` / ``{"type": "input_text", "content": ...}``

        passed through ``redact_sensitive_text``.

        when disabled the helper is effectively a no-op.

            return content
        if isinstance(content, str):

        if isinstance(content, list):

                    if isinstance(part.get("content"), str):

    def _save_session_log(self, messages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
        """Optional per-session JSON snapshot writer.

        Gated by ``sessions.write_json_snapshots`` (default False).  state.db
        is the canonical message store; this writer exists only for users
        whose external tooling consumes ``~/.hermes/sessions/session_{sid}.json``
        directly.  When the flag is off this is a fast no-op.

        When enabled, rewrites the snapshot after every persistence point with
        the full message list (assistant content normalized via
        ``_clean_session_content`` to convert REASONING_SCRATCHPAD to think
        tags).  The truncation guard ("don't overwrite a larger log with
        fewer messages") is preserved so resume + branch don't clobber a
        fuller existing snapshot.
        """
        if not getattr(self, "_session_json_enabled", False):
            return
        messages = messages or self._session_messages
        if not messages:
            return

        # Re-derive the target path each call so /branch and /compress
        # session-id changes land in the right file without any re-point
        # bookkeeping at the call sites.
        try:
            log_file = self.logs_dir / f"session_{self.session_id}.json"
        except Exception:
            return

        try:
            cleaned = []
            for msg in messages:
                if msg.get("role") == "assistant" and msg.get("content"):
                    msg = dict(msg)
                    msg["content"] = self._clean_session_content(msg["content"])
                # Defence-in-depth: redact credentials from every message
                # content before persistence. Catches PATs / API keys / Bearer
                # tokens that may have leaked into assistant responses, tool
                # output, or user paste. Respects HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS via
                # redact_sensitive_text — no-op when disabled. (#19798, #19845)
                if "content" in msg:
                    msg = dict(msg)
                    msg["content"] = self._redact_message_content(msg.get("content"))
                cleaned.append(msg)

            # Guard: never overwrite a larger session log with fewer messages.
            # Protects against data loss when a resumed agent starts with
            # partial history and would otherwise clobber the full JSON log.
            if log_file.exists():
                try:
                    existing = json.loads(log_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                    existing_count = existing.get("message_count", len(existing.get("messages", [])))
                    if existing_count > len(cleaned):
                        logging.debug(
                            "Skipping session log overwrite: existing has %d messages, current has %d",
                            existing_count, len(cleaned),
                        )
                        return
                except Exception:
                    pass  # corrupted existing file — allow the overwrite

            entry = {
                "session_id": self.session_id,
                "model": self.model,
                "base_url": self.base_url,
                "platform": self.platform,
                "session_start": self.session_start.isoformat(),
                "last_updated": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                "system_prompt": redact_sensitive_text(self._cached_system_prompt or ""),
                "tools": self.tools or [],
                "message_count": len(cleaned),
                "messages": cleaned,
            }

            atomic_json_write(
                log_file,
                entry,
                indent=2,
                default=str,
            )

        except Exception as e:
            if self.verbose_logging:
                logging.warning(f"Failed to save session log: {e}")

        Request the agent to interrupt its current tool-calling loop.
        
        Call this from another thread (e.g., input handler, message receiver)
        to gracefully stop the agent and process a new message.
        
        Also signals long-running tool executions (e.g. terminal commands)
        to terminate early, so the agent can respond immediately.

            # interrupt signal until startup completes instead of targeting
            # the caller thread by mistake.
            self._interrupt_thread_signal_pending = True

209	    """Decide whether to wait for credential-pool rotation instead of falling back.
210	
211	    The existing pool-rotation path requires the pool to (1) exist and (2) have
212	    at least one entry not currently in exhaustion cooldown.  But rotation is
213	    only meaningful when the pool has more than one entry.
214	
215	    With a single-credential pool (common for Gemini OAuth, Vertex service
216	    accounts, and any "one personal key" configuration), the primary entry
217	    just 429'd and there is nothing to rotate to.  Waiting for the pool
218	    cooldown to expire means retrying against the same exhausted quota — the
219	    daily-quota 429 will recur immediately, and the retry budget is burned.
220	
221	    Additionally, Google CloudCode / Gemini CLI rate limits are ACCOUNT-level
222	    throttles — even a multi-entry pool shares the same quota window, so
223	    rotation won't recover.  Skip straight to the fallback for those (#13636).
224	
225	    In those cases we must fall back to the configured ``fallback_model``
226	    instead.  Returns True only when rotation has somewhere to go.
227	
228	    See issues #11314 and #13636.
229	    """
230	    if pool is None:
231	        return False
232	    if not pool.has_available():
233	        return False
234	    # CloudCode / Gemini CLI quotas are account-wide — all pool entries share
235	    # the same throttle window, so rotation can't recover.  Prefer fallback.
236	    if provider == "google-gemini-cli" or str(base_url or "").startswith("cloudcode-pa://"):
237	        return False
238	    return len(pool.entries()) > 1

496	    def _transition_context_engine_session(
497	        self,
498	        *,
499	        old_session_id: Optional[str] = None,
500	        new_session_id: Optional[str] = None,
501	        previous_messages: Optional[list] = None,
502	        carry_over_context: bool = False,
503	        reset_engine: bool = True,
504	        **extra_context,
505	    ) -> None:
506	        """Notify the active context engine about a host session transition.
507	
508	        Generic host-side lifecycle helper. The built-in compressor keeps its
509	        existing reset behavior; plugin engines that implement richer hooks
510	        (``on_session_end``, ``on_session_reset``, ``on_session_start``,
511	        ``carry_over_new_session_context``) can flush old-session state,
512	        reset runtime counters, bind to the new session, and optionally
513	        carry retained context forward.
514	        """
515	        engine = getattr(self, "context_compressor", None)
516	        if not engine:
517	            return
518	
519	        if old_session_id and previous_messages is not None and hasattr(engine, "on_session_end"):
520	            try:
521	                engine.on_session_end(old_session_id, previous_messages)
522	            except Exception as exc:
523	                logger.debug("context engine on_session_end during transition: %s", exc)
524	
525	        if reset_engine and hasattr(engine, "on_session_reset"):
526	            try:
527	                engine.on_session_reset()
528	            except Exception as exc:
529	                logger.debug("context engine on_session_reset during transition: %s", exc)
530	
531	        should_start = bool(
532	            old_session_id
533	            or previous_messages is not None
534	            or carry_over_context
535	            or extra_context
536	        )
537	        target_session_id = new_session_id or getattr(self, "session_id", "") or ""
538	        if should_start and target_session_id and hasattr(engine, "on_session_start"):
539	            start_context = {
540	                "old_session_id": old_session_id,
541	                "carry_over_context": carry_over_context,
542	                "platform": getattr(self, "platform", None) or os.environ.get("HERMES_SESSION_SOURCE", "cli"),
543	                "model": getattr(self, "model", ""),
544	                "context_length": getattr(engine, "context_length", None),
545	                "conversation_id": getattr(self, "_gateway_session_key", None),
546	            }
547	            start_context.update(extra_context)
548	            start_context = {k: v for k, v in start_context.items() if v not in (None, "")}
549	            try:
550	                engine.on_session_start(target_session_id, **start_context)
551	            except Exception as exc:
552	                logger.debug("context engine on_session_start during transition: %s", exc)
553	
554	        if (
555	            carry_over_context
556	            and old_session_id
557	            and target_session_id
558	            and hasattr(engine, "carry_over_new_session_context")
559	        ):
560	            try:
561	                engine.carry_over_new_session_context(old_session_id, target_session_id)
562	            except Exception as exc:
563	                logger.debug("context engine carry_over_new_session_context during transition: %s", exc)
564

566	        self,
567	        previous_messages: Optional[list] = None,
568	        old_session_id: Optional[str] = None,
569	        carry_over_context: bool = False,
570	    ):
571	        """Reset all session-scoped token counters to 0 for a fresh session.
572	        
573	        This method encapsulates the reset logic for all session-level metrics
574	        including:
575	        - Token usage counters (input, output, total, prompt, completion)
576	        - Cache read/write tokens
577	        - API call count
578	        - Reasoning tokens
579	        - Estimated cost tracking
580	        - Context compressor internal counters
581	        
582	        The method safely handles optional attributes (e.g., context compressor)
583	        using ``hasattr`` checks.
584	
585	        When ``previous_messages`` / ``old_session_id`` / ``carry_over_context``
586	        are provided, the active context engine is notified through the
587	        full transition lifecycle (``_transition_context_engine_session``)
588	        instead of a bare reset. Default callers pass nothing and keep the
589	        existing reset-only behavior.
590	        """
591	        # Token usage counters
592	        self.session_total_tokens = 0
593	        self.session_input_tokens = 0
594	        self.session_output_tokens = 0
595	        self.session_prompt_tokens = 0
596	        self.session_completion_tokens = 0

598	        self.session_cache_write_tokens = 0
599	        self.session_reasoning_tokens = 0

655	    def _safe_print(self, *args, **kwargs):
656	        """Print that silently handles broken pipes / closed stdout.
657	
658	        In headless environments (systemd, Docker, nohup) stdout may become
659	        unavailable mid-session.  A raw ``print()`` raises ``OSError`` which
660	        can crash cron jobs and lose completed work.
661	
662	        Internally routes through ``self._print_fn`` (default: builtin
663	        ``print``) so callers such as the CLI can inject a renderer that
664	        handles ANSI escape sequences properly (e.g. prompt_toolkit's
665	        ``print_formatted_text(ANSI(...))``) without touching this method.
666	        """
667	        try:
668	            fn = self._print_fn or print
669	            fn(*args, **kwargs)
670	        except (OSError, ValueError):
671	            pass
672	
673	    def _vprint(self, *args, force: bool = False, **kwargs):
674	        """Verbose print — suppressed when actively streaming tokens.
675	
676	        Pass ``force=True`` for error/warning messages that should always be
677	        shown even during streaming playback (TTS or display).
678	
679	        During tool execution (``_executing_tools`` is True), printing is
680	        allowed even with stream consumers registered because no tokens
681	        are being streamed at that point.
682	
683	        After the main response has been delivered and the remaining tool
684	        calls are post-response housekeeping (``_mute_post_response``),
685	        all non-forced output is suppressed.
686	
687	        ``suppress_status_output`` is a stricter CLI automation mode used by
688	        parseable single-query flows such as ``hermes chat -q``. In that mode,
689	        all status/diagnostic prints routed through ``_vprint`` are suppressed
690	        so stdout stays machine-readable.
691	        """
692	        if getattr(self, "suppress_status_output", False):
693	            return
694	        if not force and getattr(self, "_mute_post_response", False):
695	            return
696	        if not force and self._has_stream_consumers() and not self._executing_tools:
697	            return
698	        self._safe_print(*args, **kwargs)

700	    def _should_start_quiet_spinner(self) -> bool:
701	        """Return True when quiet-mode spinner output has a safe sink.
702	
703	        In headless/stdio-protocol environments, a raw spinner with no custom
704	        ``_print_fn`` falls back to ``sys.stdout`` and can corrupt protocol
705	        streams such as ACP JSON-RPC. Allow quiet spinners only when either:
706	        - output is explicitly rerouted via ``_print_fn``; or
707	        - stdout is a real TTY.
708	        """
709	        if self._print_fn is not None:
710	            return True
711	        stream = getattr(sys, "stdout", None)
712	        if stream is None:
713	            return False
714	        try:
715	            return bool(stream.isatty())
716	        except (AttributeError, ValueError, OSError):
717	            return False

733	    def _emit_status(self, message: str) -> None:
734	        """Emit a lifecycle status message to both CLI and gateway channels.
735	
736	        CLI users see the message via ``_vprint(force=True)`` so it is always
737	        visible regardless of verbose/quiet mode.  Gateway consumers receive
738	        it through ``status_callback("lifecycle", ...)``.
739	
740	        This helper never raises — exceptions are swallowed so it cannot
741	        interrupt the retry/fallback logic.
742	        """
743	        try:
744	            self._vprint(f"{self.log_prefix}{message}", force=True)
745	        except Exception:
746	            pass
747	        if self.status_callback:
748	            try:
749	                self.status_callback("lifecycle", message)
750	            except Exception:
751	                logger.debug("status_callback error in _emit_status", exc_info=True)

753	    def _emit_warning(self, message: str) -> None:
754	        """Emit a user-visible warning through the same status plumbing.
755	
756	        Unlike debug logs, these warnings are meant for degraded side paths
757	        such as auxiliary compression or memory flushes where the main turn can
758	        continue but the user needs to know something important failed.
759	        """
760	        try:
761	            self._vprint(f"{self.log_prefix}{message}", force=True)
762	        except Exception:
763	            pass
764	        if self.status_callback:
765	            try:
766	                self.status_callback("warn", message)
767	            except Exception:
768	                logger.debug("status_callback error in _emit_warning", exc_info=True)

770	    # ── Buffered retry/fallback status ────────────────────────────────────
771	    # Retry and fallback chains were flooding the CLI/gateway with status
772	    # noise that users found confusing: a single transient 429 could produce
773	    # 10+ "Provider/Endpoint/Retrying in 5s..." lines before the request
774	    # eventually succeeded.  The buffered helpers below capture these
775	    # status messages instead of emitting them immediately.  They are
776	    # flushed (shown to the user) ONLY when every retry and fallback has
777	    # been exhausted; on success they are silently dropped.  Backend logs
778	    # (agent.log) are unaffected — every individual emission site still
779	    # writes to ``logger.warning`` / ``logger.info`` for diagnosis.
780	
781	    def _buffer_status(self, message: str) -> None:
782	        """Buffer a retry/fallback status message.
783	
784	        Stored as a (kind, text) tuple where ``kind`` is one of:
785	        - ``"status"``  -> replays via ``_emit_status``
786	        - ``"vprint"``  -> replays via ``_vprint(force=True)``
787	        - ``"warn"``    -> replays via ``_emit_warning``
788	        Used to defer noisy retry chatter until we know whether the
789	        turn ultimately recovered or failed.
790	        """
791	        try:
792	            buf = getattr(self, "_retry_status_buffer", None)
793	            if buf is None:
794	                buf = []
795	                self._retry_status_buffer = buf
796	            buf.append(("status", message))
797	        except Exception:
798	            # Never break the retry loop on a buffer hiccup.
799	            pass
800	
801	    def _buffer_vprint(self, message: str) -> None:
802	        """Buffer a vprint(force=True) retry/fallback line."""
803	        try:
804	            buf = getattr(self, "_retry_status_buffer", None)
805	            if buf is None:
806	                buf = []
807	                self._retry_status_buffer = buf
808	            buf.append(("vprint", message))
809	        except Exception:
810	            pass
811	
812	    def _clear_status_buffer(self) -> None:
813	        """Drop buffered retry messages — call on successful recovery."""
814	        try:
815	            buf = getattr(self, "_retry_status_buffer", None)
816	            if buf:
817	                buf.clear()
818	        except Exception:
819	            pass
820	
821	    def _flush_status_buffer(self) -> None:
822	        """Emit buffered retry messages — call on terminal failure.
823	
824	        Surfaces the full retry/fallback trace so the user can see what
825	        was tried before the turn gave up.
826	        """
827	        try:
828	            buf = getattr(self, "_retry_status_buffer", None)
829	            if not buf:
830	                return
831	            # Drain first so a callback exception doesn't double-emit.
832	            messages = list(buf)
833	            buf.clear()
834	            for kind, msg in messages:
835	                try:
836	                    if kind == "status":
837	                        self._emit_status(msg)
838	                    elif kind == "warn":
839	                        self._emit_warning(msg)
840	                    else:
841	                        self._vprint(f"{self.log_prefix}{msg}", force=True)
842	                except Exception:
843	                    pass
844	        except Exception:
845	            pass

847	    def _disable_codex_reasoning_replay(
848	        self,
849	        messages: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
850	    ) -> Dict[str, int]:
851	        """Disable Responses encrypted reasoning replay and strip cached state.
852	
853	        Called from the conversation_loop retry path when the provider
854	        rejects a replayed ``codex_reasoning_items`` blob with HTTP 400
855	        ``invalid_encrypted_content``.  Sets ``self._codex_reasoning_replay_enabled``
856	        to ``False`` (consumed by ``codex_responses_adapter._chat_messages_to_responses_input``
857	        and ``transports/codex.py`` to drop ``reasoning.encrypted_content``
858	        from subsequent requests) and pops ``codex_reasoning_items`` from
859	        every assistant message in ``messages`` so they cannot be replayed
860	        again later in the session.
861	
862	        Returns a small stats dict ``{"messages": int, "items": int}``
863	        counting what was stripped — purely for diagnostic logging.
864	        """
865	        stripped_messages = 0
866	        stripped_items = 0
867	        target_messages = messages if isinstance(messages, list) else []
868	
869	        for msg in target_messages:
870	            if not isinstance(msg, dict) or msg.get("role") != "assistant":
871	                continue
872	            items = msg.pop("codex_reasoning_items", None)
873	            if isinstance(items, list) and items:
874	                stripped_messages += 1
875	                stripped_items += len(items)
876	
877	        self._codex_reasoning_replay_enabled = False
878	        return {"messages": stripped_messages, "items": stripped_items}

905	
906	        Some Anthropic-compatible streaming providers can send a malformed
907	        event-stream frame.  The Anthropic SDK surfaces that as a plain
908	        ``ValueError`` such as ``expected ident at line 1 column 149``.  That

910	        should follow the same retry path as a truncated JSON body.

1041	    def _resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base(self) -> tuple[float, bool]:
1042	        """Resolve the base non-stream stale timeout and whether it is implicit.
1043	
1044	        Priority:
1045	          1. ``providers.<id>.models.<model>.stale_timeout_seconds``
1046	          2. ``providers.<id>.stale_timeout_seconds``
1047	          3. ``HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT`` env var
1048	          4. 90.0s default (time-to-first-byte for non-streaming / Codex
1049	             internal-streaming requests; lowered from 300s in May 2026 so
1050	             fallback providers kick in faster when upstream providers
1051	             stall).  The detector still scales up for large contexts in
1052	             ``_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout``.
1053	
1054	        Returns ``(timeout_seconds, uses_implicit_default)`` so the caller can
1055	        preserve legacy behaviors that only apply when the user has *not*
1056	        explicitly configured a stale timeout, such as auto-disabling the
1057	        detector for local endpoints.
1058	        """
1059	        cfg = get_provider_stale_timeout(self.provider, self.model)
1060	        if cfg is not None:
1061	            return cfg, False
1062	
1063	        env_timeout = os.getenv("HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT")
1064	        if env_timeout is not None:

1069	    def _compute_non_stream_stale_timeout(self, api_payload: Any) -> float:
1070	        """Compute the effective non-stream stale timeout for this request.
1071	
1072	        Accepts either the full ``api_kwargs`` dict (Chat Completions or
1073	        Responses API) or a legacy ``messages`` list.  Context-size scaling
1074	        applies the same way to both shapes via
1075	        :func:`agent.chat_completion_helpers.estimate_request_context_tokens`.
1076	        """
1077	        stale_base, uses_implicit_default = self._resolved_api_call_stale_timeout_base()
1078	        base_url = getattr(self, "_base_url", None) or self.base_url or ""
1079	        if uses_implicit_default and base_url and is_local_endpoint(base_url):
1080	            return float("inf")
1081	
1082	        from agent.chat_completion_helpers import estimate_request_context_tokens
1083	        est_tokens = estimate_request_context_tokens(api_payload)
1084	        if est_tokens > 100_000:
1085	            return max(stale_base, 240.0)
1086	        if est_tokens > 50_000:
1087	            return max(stale_base, 150.0)

1090	    def _codex_silent_hang_hint(self, model: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[str]:
1091	        """Return an actionable hint when this request matches a known
1092	        Codex silent-reject configuration, else ``None``.
1093	
1094	        The ChatGPT Codex backend (``chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex``) has
1095	        historically silently dropped certain model requests: the connection
1096	        is accepted but no stream events are emitted and no error is raised.
1097	        The stale-call detector ends the hang, but a generic "timed out"
1098	        message gives the user no path forward.
1099	
1100	        This helper substitutes an actionable hint into the stale-timeout
1101	        warning when the request matches a known silent-reject pattern.
1102	        Currently flagged: ``gpt-5.5`` family on the Codex backend.  See
1103	        hermes-agent #21444 for the symptom history.  The upstream backend
1104	        behavior has historically come and gone with ChatGPT entitlement
1105	        changes — the heuristic stays in place as future-proofing even when
1106	        the symptom is dormant.
1107	
1108	        Does NOT fix the backend issue.  Only converts an opaque stale-timeout
1109	        into actionable text so users learn the workaround in seconds rather
1110	        than digging through logs.
1111	        """
1112	        if self.api_mode != "codex_responses":
1113	            return None
1114	        is_codex_backend = (
1115	            self.provider == "openai-codex"
1116	            or (
1117	                getattr(self, "_base_url_hostname", "") == "chatgpt.com"
1118	                and "/backend-api/codex" in (getattr(self, "_base_url_lower", "") or "")
1119	            )
1120	        )
1121	        if not is_codex_backend:
1122	            return None
1123	        eff_model = (model if model is not None else self.model) or ""
1124	        model_lower = eff_model.lower()
1125	        # Match the gpt-5.5 family — bare ``gpt-5.5``, ``gpt-5.5-codex``,
1126	        # vendor-prefixed variants like ``openai/gpt-5.5``, and any future
1127	        # ``gpt-5.5-*`` SKU.  Anchor at a word boundary on either side so
1128	        # unrelated tokens like ``gpt-5.50`` do not match.
1129	        if not re.search(r"(?:^|[/\-_])gpt-5\.5(?:$|[\-_])", model_lower):
1130	            return None
1131	        return (
1132	            f"Codex backend appears to be silently rejecting {eff_model!r} "
1133	            "on chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (no stream events, no error). "
1134	            "This is a known backend-side pattern that has affected ChatGPT "
1135	            "Plus accounts intermittently. "
1136	            "Workaround: try `gpt-5.4` on the same OAuth profile, or `gpt-5.3-codex`, "
1137	            "or switch to a different model/provider in your fallback chain. "
1138	            "Some ChatGPT Codex accounts do not support `gpt-5.4-codex`. "
1139	            "See hermes-agent#21444 for symptom history."
1140	        )

1421	    def _drop_trailing_empty_response_scaffolding(self, messages: List[Dict]) -> None:
1422	        """Remove private empty-response retry/failure scaffolding from transcript tails.
1423	
1424	        Also rewinds past any trailing tool-result / assistant(tool_calls) pair
1425	        that the failed iteration left hanging. Without this, the tail ends at
1426	        a raw ``tool`` message and the next user turn lands as
1427	        ``...tool, user, user`` — a protocol-invalid sequence that most
1428	        providers silently reject (returns empty content), causing the
1429	        empty-retry loop to fire forever. See #<TBD>.
1430	        """
1431	        # Pass 1: strip the flagged scaffolding messages themselves.
1432	        dropped_scaffolding = False
1433	        while (
1434	            messages
1435	            and isinstance(messages[-1], dict)
1436	            and (
1437	                messages[-1].get("_empty_recovery_synthetic")
1438	                or messages[-1].get("_empty_terminal_sentinel")
1439	            )
1440	        ):
1441	            messages.pop()
1442	            dropped_scaffolding = True
1443	
1444	        # Pass 2: if we stripped scaffolding, rewind through any trailing
1445	        # tool-result messages plus the assistant(tool_calls) message that
1446	        # produced them. This preserves role alternation so the next user
1447	        # message follows a user or assistant message, not an orphan tool
1448	        # result. Only runs when scaffolding was actually present — normal
1449	        # conversation tails (real tool loops mid-progress) are untouched.
1450	        if not dropped_scaffolding:
1451	            return
1452	
1453	        # Drop any trailing tool-result messages
1454	        while (
1455	            messages
1456	            and isinstance(messages[-1], dict)

1594	    @staticmethod
1595	    def _is_entitlement_failure(
1596	        error_context: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
1597	        status_code: Optional[int],
1598	    ) -> bool:
1599	        """Detect subscription/entitlement 403s that masquerade as auth failures.
1600	
1601	        Returned True only when the body text matches a known entitlement
1602	        shape AND the status is 401/403.  Refreshing an OAuth token cannot
1603	        fix an unsubscribed account, so callers should surface the error
1604	        instead of looping the credential pool.
1605	
1606	        Current matches:
1607	          * xAI OAuth: "do not have an active Grok subscription" /
1608	            "out of available resources" / "does not have permission" + "grok"
1609	
1610	        Disambiguator for xAI (#29344): the same ``code`` text ("The caller
1611	        does not have permission to execute the specified operation") is
1612	        returned for BOTH an unsubscribed account AND a stale OAuth access
1613	        token.  xAI ships an explicit signal in the ``error`` field that
1614	        tells the two apart: a ``[WKE=unauthenticated:...]`` suffix (and/or
1615	        the ``OAuth2 access token could not be validated`` phrasing) means
1616	        the credentials failed validation — that's recoverable by refreshing
1617	        the token, NOT by surfacing an entitlement message.  When either
1618	        signal is present we return False eagerly so the credential-pool
1619	        refresh path runs, letting long-running TUI sessions recover from
1620	        stale tokens without an exit/reopen cycle.
1621	
1622	        Extend here for new providers as we discover them (Anthropic's
1623	        Claude Max OAuth entitlement errors look distinct enough today that
1624	        the existing 1M-context-beta branch handles them; revisit if other
1625	        subscription tiers start producing the same loop signature).
1626	        """
1627	        if status_code not in {401, 403, None}:
1628	            return False
1629	        if not isinstance(error_context, dict):
1630	            return False
1631	        # Build a single lowercase haystack covering every field shape the
1632	        # body might land in.  ``_extract_api_error_context`` normalises to
1633	        # ``message``/``reason``, but callers (and the test suite) may also
1634	        # hand us the raw body with ``code``/``error`` keys; cover both so
1635	        # the WKE disambiguator below fires regardless of entry point.
1636	        message = str(error_context.get("message") or "").lower()
1637	        reason = str(error_context.get("reason") or "").lower()
1638	        code = str(error_context.get("code") or "").lower()
1639	        err = str(error_context.get("error") or "").lower()
1640	        haystack = f"{message} {reason} {code} {err}"
1641	        if not haystack.strip():
1642	            return False
1643	        # xAI's authoritative disambiguator for "stale token" vs
1644	        # "unsubscribed account".  Both conditions share the same
1645	        # permission-denied ``code`` text; only one carries this suffix.
1646	        # Bail out before the entitlement keyword checks so a stale OAuth
1647	        # token routes through the credential-refresh path instead of the
1648	        # surface-error-as-entitlement path.  See #29344 for the long-
1649	        # running TUI failure mode this closes.
1650	        if "[wke=unauthenticated:" in haystack:
1651	            return False
1652	        if "oauth2 access token could not be validated" in haystack:
1653	            return False
1654	        if "do not have an active grok subscription" in haystack:
1655	            return True
1656	        if "out of available resources" in haystack and "grok" in haystack:
1657	            return True
1658	        if "does not have permission" in haystack and "grok" in haystack:
1659	            return True
1660	        return False

1662	    @staticmethod
1663	    def _decorate_xai_entitlement_error(detail: str) -> str:
1664	        """Append a neutral hint when xAI's OAuth surface returns the
1665	        permission-denied 403.
1666	
1667	        xAI's ``/v1/responses`` endpoint replies to several distinct failure
1668	        modes with the SAME body::
1669	
1670	            {"code": "The caller does not have permission to execute the
1671	             specified operation", "error": "You have either run out of
1672	             available resources or do not have an active Grok subscription.
1673	             Manage subscriptions at https://grok.com/?_s=usage or subscribe
1674	             at https://grok.com/supergrok"}
1675	
1676	        That body covers several real causes we cannot distinguish without
1677	        more info from xAI.  The most common (and least obvious) one is
1678	        that **X Premium+ does NOT include API access** — only standalone
1679	        SuperGrok subscribers can use Hermes against xai-oauth.  Lots of
1680	        users see Grok in their X app, assume it works here too, and hit
1681	        this 403 with no idea why.  Lead the hint with that.
1682	
1683	        Other possible causes:
1684	          * No Grok subscription at all
1685	          * SuperGrok tier doesn't include the requested model (e.g.
1686	            grok-4.3 may need a higher tier)
1687	          * Monthly quota exhausted (the ``?_s=usage`` URL hints at this)
1688	
1689	        Surface the raw xAI text verbatim and point at
1690	        https://grok.com/?_s=usage where the user can see WHICH applies.
1691	
1692	        Matched once per detail string — won't double-decorate if the
1693	        upstream already concatenated the same text.
1694	        """
1695	        if not detail:
1696	            return detail
1697	        lower = detail.lower()
1698	        is_entitlement = (
1699	            "do not have an active grok subscription" in lower
1700	            or ("out of available resources" in lower and "grok" in lower)
1701	            or ("does not have permission" in lower and "grok" in lower)
1702	        )
1703	        if not is_entitlement:
1704	            return detail
1705	        hint = (
1706	            " — xAI rejected this OAuth account. NOTE: X Premium+ does NOT "
1707	            "include xAI API access — only standalone SuperGrok subscribers "
1708	            "can use this provider. Other possible causes: no Grok "
1709	            "subscription, your tier doesn't include this model, or your "
1710	            "quota is exhausted. Check https://grok.com/?_s=usage to see "
1711	            "which, or run `/model` to switch providers."
1712	        )
1713	        # Idempotency: detect prior decoration by a substring unique to the
1714	        # hint (not present in xAI's own body text).
1715	        if "X Premium+ does NOT include" in detail:
1716	            return detail
1717	        return f"{detail}{hint}"

1719	    @staticmethod
1720	    def _summarize_api_error(error: Exception) -> str:
1721	        """Extract a human-readable one-liner from an API error.
1722	
1723	        Handles Cloudflare HTML error pages (502, 503, etc.) by pulling the
1724	        <title> tag instead of dumping raw HTML.  Falls back to a truncated
1725	        str(error) for everything else.
1726	        """
1727	        raw = str(error)
1728	
1729	        if (
1730	            isinstance(error, ValueError)
1731	            and "expected ident at line" in raw.lower()
1732	        ):
1733	            return f"Malformed provider streaming response: {raw[:300]}"
1734	
1735	        # Cloudflare / proxy HTML pages: grab the <title> for a clean summary
1736	        if "<!DOCTYPE" in raw or "<html" in raw:
1737	            m = re.search(r"<title[^>]*>([^<]+)</title>", raw, re.IGNORECASE)
1738	            title = m.group(1).strip() if m else "HTML error page (title not found)"
1739	            # Also grab Cloudflare Ray ID if present
1740	            ray = re.search(r"Cloudflare Ray ID:\s*<strong[^>]*>([^<]+)</strong>", raw)
1741	            ray_id = ray.group(1).strip() if ray else None
1742	            status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
1743	            parts = []
1744	            if status_code:
1745	                parts.append(f"HTTP {status_code}")
1746	            parts.append(title)
1747	            if ray_id:
1748	                parts.append(f"Ray {ray_id}")
1749	            return " — ".join(parts)
1750	
1751	        # JSON body errors from OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs
1752	        body = getattr(error, "body", None)
1753	        if isinstance(body, dict):
1754	            msg = body.get("error", {}).get("message") if isinstance(body.get("error"), dict) else body.get("message")
1755	            if msg:
1756	                status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
1757	                prefix = f"HTTP {status_code}: " if status_code else ""
1758	                return AIAgent._decorate_xai_entitlement_error(f"{prefix}{msg[:300]}")
1759	
1760	        # Fallback: truncate the raw string but give more room than 200 chars
1761	        status_code = getattr(error, "status_code", None)
1762	        prefix = f"HTTP {status_code}: " if status_code else ""
1763	        return AIAgent._decorate_xai_entitlement_error(f"{prefix}{raw[:500]}")

1875	    def _save_session_log(self, messages: List[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
1876	        """Optional per-session JSON snapshot writer.
1877	
1878	        Gated by ``sessions.write_json_snapshots`` (default False).  state.db
1879	        is the canonical message store; this writer exists only for users
1880	        whose external tooling consumes ``~/.hermes/sessions/session_{sid}.json``
1881	        directly.  When the flag is off this is a fast no-op.
1882	
1883	        When enabled, rewrites the snapshot after every persistence point with
1884	        the full message list (assistant content normalized via
1885	        ``_clean_session_content`` to convert REASONING_SCRATCHPAD to think
1886	        tags).  The truncation guard ("don't overwrite a larger log with
1887	        fewer messages") is preserved so resume + branch don't clobber a
1888	        fuller existing snapshot.
1889	        """
1890	        if not getattr(self, "_session_json_enabled", False):
1891	            return
1892	        messages = messages or self._session_messages
1893	        if not messages:
1894	            return
1895	
1896	        # Re-derive the target path each call so /branch and /compress
1897	        # session-id changes land in the right file without any re-point
1898	        # bookkeeping at the call sites.
1899	        try:
1900	            log_file = self.logs_dir / f"session_{self.session_id}.json"
1901	        except Exception:
1902	            return
1903	
1904	        try:
1905	            cleaned = []
1906	            for msg in messages:
1907	                if msg.get("role") == "assistant" and msg.get("content"):
1908	                    msg = dict(msg)
1909	                    msg["content"] = self._clean_session_content(msg["content"])
1910	                # Defence-in-depth: redact credentials from every message
1911	                # content before persistence. Catches PATs / API keys / Bearer
1912	                # tokens that may have leaked into assistant responses, tool
1913	                # output, or user paste. Respects HERMES_REDACT_SECRETS via
1914	                # redact_sensitive_text — no-op when disabled. (#19798, #19845)
1915	                if "content" in msg:
1916	                    msg = dict(msg)
1917	                    msg["content"] = self._redact_message_content(msg.get("content"))
1918	                cleaned.append(msg)
1919	
1920	            # Guard: never overwrite a larger session log with fewer messages.
1921	            # Protects against data loss when a resumed agent starts with
1922	            # partial history and would otherwise clobber the full JSON log.
1923	            if log_file.exists():
1924	                try:
1925	                    existing = json.loads(log_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
1926	                    existing_count = existing.get("message_count", len(existing.get("messages", [])))
1927	                    if existing_count > len(cleaned):
1928	                        logging.debug(
1929	                            "Skipping session log overwrite: existing has %d messages, current has %d",
1930	                            existing_count, len(cleaned),
1931	                        )
1932	                        return
1933	                except Exception:
1934	                    pass  # corrupted existing file — allow the overwrite
1935	
1936	            entry = {
1937	                "session_id": self.session_id,
1938	                "model": self.model,
1939	                "base_url": self.base_url,
1940	                "platform": self.platform,
1941	                "session_start": self.session_start.isoformat(),
1942	                "last_updated": datetime.now().isoformat(),
1943	                "system_prompt": redact_sensitive_text(self._cached_system_prompt or ""),
1944	                "tools": self.tools or [],
1945	                "message_count": len(cleaned),
1946	                "messages": cleaned,
1947	            }
1948	
1949	            atomic_json_write(
1950	                log_file,
1951	                entry,
1952	                indent=2,
1953	                default=str,
1954	            )
1955	
1956	        except Exception as e:
1957	            if self.verbose_logging:
1958	                logging.warning(f"Failed to save session log: {e}")

1961	    def interrupt(self, message: str = None) -> None:
1962	        """
1963	        Request the agent to interrupt its current tool-calling loop.
1964	        
1965	        Call this from another thread (e.g., input handler, message receiver)
1966	        to gracefully stop the agent and process a new message.
1967	        
1968	        Also signals long-running tool executions (e.g. terminal commands)
1969	        to terminate early, so the agent can respond immediately.
1970	        
1971	        Args:
1972	            message: Optional new message that triggered the interrupt.
1973	                     If provided, the agent will include this in its response context.
1974	        
1975	        Example (CLI):
1976	            # In a separate input thread:
1977	            if user_typed_something:
1978	                agent.interrupt(user_input)
1979	        
1980	        Example (Messaging):
1981	            # When new message arrives for active session:
1982	            if session_has_running_agent:
1983	                running_agent.interrupt(new_message.text)
1984	        """
1985	        self._interrupt_requested = True
1986	        self._interrupt_message = message
1987	        # Signal all tools to abort any in-flight operations immediately.
1988	        # Scope the interrupt to this agent's execution thread so other
1989	        # agents running in the same process (gateway) are not affected.

1993	        else:

1995	            # binding the agent to its execution thread. Defer the tool-level
1996	            # interrupt signal until startup completes instead of targeting
1997	            # the caller thread by mistake.
1998	            self._interrupt_thread_signal_pending = True

def _pool_may_recover_from_rate_limit(
    pool, *, provider: str | None = None, base_url: str | None = None
) -> bool:
    """Decide whether to wait for credential-pool rotation instead of falling back.

    The existing pool-rotation path requires the pool to (1) exist and (2) have
    at least one entry not currently in exhaustion cooldown.  But rotation is
    only meaningful when the pool has more than one entry.

    With a single-credential pool (common for Gemini OAuth, Vertex service
    accounts, and any "one personal key" configuration), the primary entry
    just 429'd and there is nothing to rotate to.  Waiting for the pool
    cooldown to expire means retrying against the same exhausted quota — the
    daily-quota 429 will recur immediately, and the retry budget is burned.

    Additionally, Google CloudCode / Gemini CLI rate limits are ACCOUNT-level
    throttles — even a multi-entry pool shares the same quota window, so
    rotation won't recover.  Skip straight to the fallback for those (#13636).

    In those cases we must fall back to the configured ``fallback_model``
    instead.  Returns True only when rotation has somewhere to go.

    See issues #11314 and #13636.
    """
    if pool is None:
        return False
    if not pool.has_available():
        return False
    # CloudCode / Gemini CLI quotas are account-wide — all pool entries share
    # the same throttle window, so rotation can't recover.  Prefer fallback.
    if provider == "google-gemini-cli" or str(base_url or "").startswith("cloudcode-pa://"):
        return False
    return len(pool.entries()) > 1

class _StreamErrorEvent(Exception):
    """Synthesized provider error surfaced from a Responses ``error`` SSE frame.

    Some Codex-style Responses backends (xAI for subscription/quota
    failures, custom relays under malformed-tool-call conditions) emit a
    standalone ``type=error`` frame instead of routing the failure
    through ``response.failed`` or returning an HTTP 4xx.  The fallback
    streaming path raises this exception so ``_summarize_api_error`` and
    ``_extract_api_error_context`` see a familiar ``.body`` /
    ``.status_code`` shape and the entitlement detector can match the
    underlying provider message ("do not have an active Grok
    subscription", etc.).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        message: str,
        *,
        code: Optional[str] = None,
        param: Optional[str] = None,
        status_code: Optional[int] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.code = code
        self.param = param
        self.status_code = status_code
        # OpenAI SDK-shaped body so _extract_api_error_context /
        # _summarize_api_error / classify_api_error all pick it up.
        self.body: Dict[str, Any] = {
            "error": {
                "message": message,
                "code": code,
                "param": param,
                "type": "error",
            }
        }
